observation_summary: The Joda-Time library throws an IllegalFieldValueException when performing date arithmetic that crosses the 1 BC to 1 AD boundary, because it encounters a year 0, which is not supported in the Julian/Gregorian calendar systems.
reasoning_summary: The issue is that the internal date arithmetic logic (specifically in GJChronology and JulianChronology) does not correctly handle the transition across the year 0 boundary. The code explicitly throws an exception when it encounters year 0, but the library's design goal is to skip year 0 automatically. This is a procedural logic error in how the chronology handles year transitions, requiring an adjustment to the calculation algorithm rather than a simple guard or a design-level change.
evidence_used: org.joda.time.IllegalFieldValueException: Value 0 for year is not supported

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the code contains a check that throws an exception, the root cause is the failure of the arithmetic algorithm to account for the missing year 0, not just the presence of the check itself.
The capability to handle dates exists, but the specific implementation of the year-skipping logic is flawed, which is a procedural/algorithmic issue.
